question: Should localization governance be a closed core-owned inventory of every product, channel, plugin, and skill surface, or should core expose only generic validation while each owner declares its own localization evidence?
rationale: The choice fixes the long-term plugin and channel ownership contract, so it cannot safely be inferred from a contributor implementation alone.

options.title: Use generic core aggregation
options.body: Keep shared schema and validation primitives in core, but have each owner publish its own surface declaration through an established manifest or SDK seam.

options.title: Adopt the closed core registry
options.body: Accept that adding or changing a covered owner surface requires coordinated edits to the central required-surface union and repository-wide gate.

options.title: Pause the governance slice
options.body: Defer this slice until the localization RFC has an explicit maintainer decision on owner boundaries and release claims.

recommendation.title: Use generic core aggregation
recommendation.body: Keep shared schema and validation primitives in core, but have each owner publish its own surface declaration through an established manifest or SDK seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal and linked RFC define the intended governance model; a repository product owner should make the final acceptance decision after that clarification.
